findings.title: Add executable duplicate-report preflight
findings.why_it_matters: A production database containing two historical reports with the same request and reason will cause the new unique-index build to abort, leaving the release migration unapplied. The runbook names this as a No-Go condition but does not provide an executable check, so an operator cannot reliably prove the migration is safe before the deploy window. A read-only preflight that fails the rollout when it returns rows makes the gate observable without deleting report history automatically.
findings.suggested_fix: Add this required preflight to the release runbook or a checked-in release script and block the migration if it returns rows: SELECT request_id, reason, COUNT(*) AS duplicate_count FROM la_chung_reports GROUP BY request_id, reason HAVING COUNT(*) > 1; Resolve each duplicate set under the retention policy, then rerun the query and the PostgreSQL migration-up check before deploying.
evidence: apps/api/migrations/versions/20260904_0008_identity_la_chung.py:90-103 -- la_chung_reports was created with only the non-unique ix_la_chung_report_request_created index.

docs/operations/chart-synthesis-release-runbook.md:29 -- Before migration `20260907_0012`, preflight confirms there are no duplicate Lá Chứng reports for the same `(request_id, reason)`; resolve duplicates before creating the unique index.

residual_risks: PostgreSQL migration up/down and the two-worker lease/CAS test remain explicit No-Go release gates; the local runbook reports Docker/PostgreSQL unavailable on this machine.
testing_gaps: No checked-in PostgreSQL migration fixture demonstrates that the duplicate-report preflight catches existing duplicates before 20260907_0012 attempts its unique-index build.
